metadata.title: Simply connected quotients of fake quadrics
metadata.abstract: Fake quadrics are minimal complex surfaces of general type with $b_1=0$ and $e=4$. The paper gives a short introduction to their arithmetic construction, aimed at low-dimensional topologists, and studies their holomorphic and antiholomorphic quotients and their fundamental groups. The running example in the paper comes from a quaternion algebra over a totally real cubic field. The lattice is generated by three explicit pairs of matrices. A holomorphic involution gives (after resolving the singularities) a simply connected minimal complex surface of general type with $p_g=0$ and $K^2=4$, a smooth $4$-manifold homeomorphic but non-diffeomorphic to $CP^2$ blown up $5$ times. An antiholomorphic involution gives a smooth four-manifold homeomorphic to $S^4$, with a knotted torus as branch locus.

metadata.title: Local Aronson-Bénilan estimates for the porous medium and fast diffusion equations on collapsing manifolds
metadata.abstract: We establish local Aronson-Bénilan estimates for positive solutions to the porous medium and fast diffusion equations on complete noncompact Riemannian manifolds with a small scale-invariant integral bound on the negative part of the Ricci curvature in $L^p$, where $p>n/2$. No uniform lower bound on the volume of unit balls is assumed, and hence the results apply to manifolds that may collapse. For the fast diffusion equation, we obtain the estimate in the range $1-2/n<m<1$. The auxiliary function method, which was designed for the heat equation under integral curvature conditions, is not directly applicable to those two nonlinear equations. The pressure operator in both cases contains a solution-dependent coefficient, which produces a residual term involving $\partial_t J$ in the evolution inequality. Its treatment requires a positive lower bound for $J$, and moreover, control of $-\partial_t\log J$. We obtain these bounds by linearizing the auxiliary equation, applying Duhamel's formula, and combining local Dirichlet heat kernel estimates with a singular Volterra inequality. Additionally, in the fast diffusion case, the negativity of $v$ changes the sign structure of the evolution inequality, so a separate coercive estimate is required to close the argument. Local Aronson-Bénilan estimates follow for both diffusion regimes and integrating them along space-time curves gives the corresponding Harnack inequalities.

metadata.title: Strong unique continuation on Riemannian manifolds for degenerate elliptic operators with convexified weights
metadata.abstract: In this manuscript, we consider a degenerate elliptic equation on a Riemannian manifold whose weight vanishes at an interior point $p$, and prove the strong unique continuation property (SUCP) at $p$. The curved setting gives rise to intrinsic geometric error terms that obstruct the analytic estimates available in the Euclidean case. To overcome this, we introduce a convexified radial weight that restores coercivity in the Carleman commutator. Combining the resulting Carleman estimate with a Hardy-type inequality and a Caccioppoli inequality, we show that any weak solution vanishing to infinite order at the degeneracy point must be identically zero on the connected domain. This result is the first SUCP theorem for this class of degenerate operators on general Riemannian manifolds.

metadata.title: Parabolic frequency and backward uniqueness on compact Finsler metric measure spaces
metadata.abstract: We establish monotonicity formulas for parabolic frequency functions on closed Finsler metric measure spaces with fixed or evolving metrics and measures. When the reference measure is fixed, an integral bound on the metric variation yields monotonicity for the Finsler heat equation. For coupled metric measure flows, we construct positive global supersolutions and subsolutions of a linearized conjugate heat equation from local radial barriers. These weights define a frequency function whose monotonicity follows from an integral bound involving the metric variation and the change in weighted Ricci curvature. For parabolic equations with a source controlled by the solution and its gradient, we obtain a differential inequality for the frequency and prove that a solution vanishing at the terminal time must vanish throughout the preceding interval. The proof controls the comparison of the two weights through an energy quotient computed with the subsolution measure.

metadata.title: Coefficient Riemann--Hilbert for an Affine Singular Foliation
metadata.abstract: For the affine foliation $\langle x\partial_x,y\partial_x\rangle$, we prove that smooth coefficient integration is a strictly unital $A_\infty$ quasi-equivalence on every ordinary open subset of $\mathbb R^2$, for globally bounded, degreewise finite-projective real coefficient bodies, allowing internal cohomology of nonconstant rank. A horizontal-hull restriction of a finite Lie $2$-groupoid model admits a smooth simplicial section of the comparison from full Maurer--Cartan integration, with a homotopy relative to all unit-generated simplices. Strict differentiation and two relative Hom models yield a real-linear chain map whose internal-degree diagonal is the identity. Its inverse is a finite sum acting directly on the possibly rank-jumping body complex. Global acyclicity of the differentiation kernels gives invertible counits that are the identity on the body. Infinitely flat and nongeneric rank-jumping examples illustrate the nonregular theorem. Separately, regular two-term coefficients admit a residue classification and an exact ordinary-quotient descent criterion. Nonzero residue obstructs pullback through any strict map to an ordinary groupoid nerve with represented objects in the stated raw coefficient theory. For regular vertical families over $S\times\mathbb R^2$, we also prove a finite-projective bundle-valued theorem natural under smooth parameter pullback; its two-term invariants are bundle arrows, rather than pointwise rank profiles.

metadata.title: Rigidity of spacelike graphs in generalized Robertson-Walker spacetimes via the infinity-Laplacian
metadata.abstract: In the search for new characterizations of spacelike slices in generalized Robertson-Walker spacetimes, we introduce a new approach. The main tool for addressing this question is the infty-Laplacian with respect to the Riemannian metric induced on the spacelike hypersurface, together with a Liouville-type property for the infinity-Laplacian on any complete Riemannian manifold by Araujo, Mari and Pessoa in 2021. Starting from the infinity-Laplacian of the height function of a spacelike hypersurface, we derive several differential equations involving the infinity-Laplacian of suitable compositions of the height function, namely, the warping function f(h), its primitive P=\int f, and the logarithmic composition log(f(h)). Under some natural assumptions, including timelike and null energy conditions, global rigidity results are established in the parametric setting. Some of these results specialize naturally to complete spacelike hypersurfaces in the Steady State spacetime and in Einstein-de Sitter spacetime. Finally, we consider a second-order PDE involving the infty-Laplacian and study the uniqueness of its entire solutions on the fiber of the generalized Robertson-Walker spacetime. This leads to new Calabi-Bernstein-type uniqueness results in the non-parametric setting.

metadata.title: Cobordism maps and Atiyah-Floer isomorphisms for framed instanton homology I
metadata.abstract: We prove that isomorphisms of the type constructed by Daemi, Fukaya and Lipyanskiy, between framed instanton homology and the Lagrangian Floer homology of a Heegaard splitting, intertwine the cobordism maps of Kronheimer and Mrowka with maps defined by holomorphic curves alone, over the field of two elements. This holds for every connected cobordism between connected three-manifolds carrying a framed arc between its ends and an $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ bundle trivialized along the ends and the arc. The symplectic maps count holomorphic triangles in moduli spaces of flat connections on surfaces, with the correspondence of a compression body as boundary condition for one- and three-handles. metadata.title: Classification of real Lie algebras of dimension six
metadata.abstract: We summarize a coordinate-free classification of six-dimensional real Lie algebras up to isomorphism. Instead of solving the overdetermined Jacobi system of 120 quadratic equations on 90 structure constants modulo $\mathrm{GL}(6,\mathbb{R})$, the method uses the Levi--Malcev decomposition, Mostow's nilradical constraints, and the Skjelbred--Sund cohomological central extension technique. In the semisimple sector, the four real forms of $A_1\oplus A_1$ are classified by Killing signature invariants, with explicit matrix representatives for $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb{C})_{\mathbb{R}}\cong\mathfrak{so}(3,1)$. For non-solvable algebras with three-dimensional radical, representation-theoretic rigidity shows that $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ cannot couple indecomposably with non-abelian radicals, yielding exactly three indecomposable classes governed by $\mathfrak{so}(3)$ and $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb{R})$. In the solvable category, Mostow's theorem restricts the nilradical dimension to $\{3,4,5,6\}$. The nilpotent sector in dimension six has twenty-four indecomposable isomorphism classes plus decomposable counterparts. Solvable non-nilpotent algebras are classified by nilradical codimension, with explicit real Jordan matrix representations for codimension one and two that resolve continuous moduli under gauge actions. The work also computes the minimal faithful representation dimension $\mu(\mathfrak{g})$ under Ado's theorem, relates the classification to invariant complex structures on nilmanifolds, and provides a deterministic, page-breakable identification algorithm.

metadata.title: On deformations of foliated complex analytic structures IV-1: Obstructed and unobstructed foliated deformations
metadata.abstract: We study obstructions of deformations of foliated complex analytic structures. We describe obstructions in terms of Cech resolutions. From foliated complex analytic families in Part I and unfolded complex analytic families in Part III, we deduce the integrability conditions. We identify infinitesimal deformations and obstructions in terms of Dolbeault resolutions or Dolbeault type bicomplexes from the integrability conditions. Then we describe the correspondences of infinitesimal deformations and obstructions between Cech resolutions, and Dolbeault resolutions or Dolbeault type bicomplexes.

metadata.title: The inscribed $4$-polytope of maximal volume with nine vertices
metadata.abstract: We prove that a $4$-polytope with nine vertices inscribed in the unit sphere $\mathbb{S}^{3}$ has volume at most $\frac{5}{24}\sqrt{10 + 2\sqrt{5}}$, and that, up to orthogonal transformations, equality holds only for the convex hull of a square and a regular pentagon inscribed in $\mathbb{S}^{3}$ in orthogonal $2$-planes through the origin. For the combinatorial type of this polytope, whose boundary complex is the join of a $4$-cycle and a $5$-cycle, we write the signed volume as the pairing, through the Hodge star, of the area vectors of the two cycles, and bound each area vector by finite Fourier analysis; the bound holds for every choice of nine points on the sphere. Since an optimal polytope is simplicial, by a result of Horváth and Lángi, it remains to exclude the other simplicial types, which we do by sum-of-squares certificates checked in exact arithmetic.

metadata.title: On the index of two-dimensional elliptic end-periodic operators
metadata.abstract: This paper investigates the index problem for elliptic end-periodic differential operators on a two-dimensional manifold with a cylindrical end. We define the topological index as the sum of the contribution of the interior symbol, expressed by an Atiyah--Singer type integral, and the contribution of the limit operator, expressed in terms of the Melrose type eta-invariant and a correction term that depends on the lower order terms of the limit operator. We prove the homotopy invariance of the topological index, which allows us to reduce the original problem to the study of operators of a simpler form by employing $K$-theoretic methods.

metadata.title: The Whitney Extension Problem in Carnot groups
metadata.abstract: Let $\mathbb{G}$ be a Carnot group, let $E \subset \mathbb{G}$ be compact, and suppose we are given a function $f: E \to \mathbb{R}$. The $C^1_H$ {\em Whitney Extension Problem} asks the following: what must be true about $f$ to guarantee that there exists a smooth, horizontal function $F \in C^1_H(\mathbb{G})$ extending $f$, i.e., there is some $F:\mathbb{G} \to \mathbb{R}$ such that $F|_E = f|_E$ and $XF$ is continuous for every horizontal left invariant vector field $X$? We adapt the method of G. Glaeser and C. Fefferman to answer this question in this non-commutative setting. Moreover, we provide an alternative solution to the $C^1$ Whitney Extension Problem for horizontal curves in the Heisenberg group.

metadata.title: Liftable braid factorizations from line arrangements: Hironaka's relations and a Zariski pair
metadata.abstract: We realize Hironaka's generalized lantern relations by lifting positive braid factorizations. For a nonpencil real line arrangement with no parallel lines, we construct a family of branched coverings on the regular fibers of a blown-up pencil of spheres. The motion of the branch points gives a factorization of a power of the full twist into least liftable powers of half-twists. The Artal-Carmona-Cogolludo-Marco Zariski pair gives two such factorizations of the same braid for a single simple branched covering of the disk. Their lifts are Hurwitz inequivalent even up to simultaneous conjugation by page homeomorphisms. The corresponding Milnor fibers fill the same planar contact three-manifold and have the same incidence matrix. They are homeomorphic and lie in distinct strong symplectic deformation classes.

metadata.title: Polynomial conjugacy invariants of pseudo-Anosov maps derived from train track representatives
metadata.abstract: We investigate two kinds of polynomials associated with pseudo-Anosov maps. Each kind consists of three polynomials that are conjugacy invariants of pseudo-Anosov mapping classes and these polynomials contain more information than pseudo-Anosov stretch factors. The first kind is defined by the train track representatives. The second kind is obtained from the first kind by incorporating additional data that encode the transitions among the unpunctured singularities of the invariant foliations. The Birman-Brinkmann-Kawamuro polynomials coincide with those of the second kind. As an application, we prove that the Birman-Brinkmann-Kawamuro polynomials are conjugacy invariants of pseudo-Anosov mapping classes which is also proved by Dodge-Kawamuro, independently.

analysisBasis.abstract: We investigate two kinds of polynomials associated with pseudo-Anosov maps. Each kind consists of three polynomials that are conjugacy invariants of pseudo-Anosov mapping classes and these polynomials contain more information than pseudo-Anosov stretch factors. The first kind is defined by the train track representatives. The second kind is obtained from the first kind by incorporating additional data that encode the transitions among the unpunctured singularities of the invariant foliations. The Birman-Brinkmann-Kawamuro polynomials coincide with those of the second kind. As an application, we prove that the Birman-Brinkmann-Kawamuro polynomials are conjugacy invariants of pseudo-Anosov mapping classes which is also proved by Dodge-Kawamuro, independently.

metadata.title: Uniqueness and stability of Appleton's solitons
metadata.abstract: We prove that Appleton's noncollapsed steady gradient Ricci solitons on complex line bundles over positive Kähler--Einstein manifolds are the unique such solitons arising from his metric ansatz. We then show that the four-dimensional examples on $O_{\mathbb{CP}^1}(-k)$, $k \geq 3$, are strictly linearly stable. By a result of Deruelle, this implies dynamical stability under the Ricci flow.

metadata.title: The Fast Tree Transform
metadata.abstract: The Fast Tree Transform is a locally-aggregated transform defined for arbitrary graph geometries that generalizes both the Hadamard frequency transform and the Haar wavelet transform on the circle. The pure frequency part of the transform approximately diagonalizes the graph Laplacian; this fact makes it useful as a preconditioner in geometric optimization problems. The full transform provides an only slightly-redundant representation of signals on the graph that allows sparse representation of signals that include both edges and textures.

metadata.title: An exact Kähler form on $(\mathbb C^*)^2$ without a global SYZ fibration
metadata.abstract: We construct an explicit exact Kähler form on \((\mathbb C^*)^2\) admitting no almost-toric fibration and hence no smooth Lagrangian torus fibration. For the logarithmic holomorphic volume form, we also rule out any special Lagrangian fibrations with compact fibers and dense regular locus, even when arbitrary compact connected singular fibers are allowed. For higher dimensions, taking products also yields explicit exact Kähler forms on \((\mathbb C^*)^n\), for every \(n\ge2\), admitting no smooth proper Lagrangian torus fibration.

metadata.title: Local regularity and p-harmonic approximation for weak inverse mean curvature flow
metadata.abstract: We prove local Lipschitz regularity for locally bounded $BV$ solutions of the calibration equations for inverse mean curvature flow. We also approximate every prescribed variational weak flow locally by Moser's logarithmic transforms of positive $p$-harmonic functions. On a fixed smooth domain, with the trace of a calibrated Lipschitz solution prescribed, both the uniform error and the absolute difference of total variations are $O((p-1)^{1/3})$ as $p\downarrow1$. In particular, the approximations converge strictly in $BV$.

metadata.title: Positive sectional curvature on all smooth 13-spheres
metadata.abstract: Every smooth homotopy $13$-sphere admits a Riemannian metric of strictly positive sectional curvature. We construct a special $S^3$--$S^3$ bundle over $S^{13}$ whose star quotient represents the nonzero class $\pm\alpha_1\beta_1\in\Theta_{13}\cong\mathbb Z/3$. The defining equivariant map factors through the Blakers--Massey map by a smooth Hopf construction representing an unstable $J$-generator. This factorisation retains the prescribed base representation and makes Schultz's plumbing composition formula applicable; a normal-invariant computation in smoothing theory then identifies the smooth structure. On the quotient we implement the compatible-disk strategy with complete curvature estimates on arbitrary two-planes, matching boundary metrics, and a strictly positive sum of outward second fundamental forms. A direct smoothing argument completes the metric construction. Orientation reversal gives the remaining nonzero class in $\Theta_{13}$.

metadata.title: Confronting Uncertainty in Mechanism-AI Coupled Dynamical Systems via Optimal Transport and Information Geometry: Part I. Distribution Learning
metadata.abstract: Mechanism-AI coupled dynamical systems are increasingly used to study complex biological systems. However, uncertainty associated with noisy, sparse, and partially observed data limits their reliability. This paper presents a systematic mathematical formulation for treating these uncertainties from the perspective of optimal transport and information geometry. We formulate the uncertainty quantification problem as the minimization of an energy functional on a probability density space equipped with a Riemannian metric, with the loss evaluated through a differential equation, and give a unified description of the gradient flows of the energy functional under specific metrics, such as the Wasserstein and Fisher-Rao metrics. Furthermore, we present corresponding numerical methods for solving these gradient flows using abstract adjoint sensitivity analysis. The formulation connects a range of Bayesian inference methods for dynamical systems; numerical experiments compare posterior approximation and predictive uncertainty under a common computational budget. Moreover, it also provides a geometric perspective on dynamical modeling and the study of heterogeneity evolution.

metadata.title: Curvature estimates for stable hypersurfaces of the Euler-Dierkes-Huisken functional
metadata.abstract: A hypersurface $\Sigma \subset\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ is called EDH-stable if it is a critical point of the Euler-Dierkes-Huisken functional $\mathcal{E}_\alpha(\Sigma)=\int_\Sigma|x|^\alpha\, d\mathcal{H}^n$ with nonnegative second variation, which was introduced by Dierkes and Huisken in \cite{[DH-24]}. In this paper, we first establish a Bellettini-type $\epsilon$-regularity theorem and use it, together with tangent cone analysis, to derive curvature estimates for EDH-stable hypersurfaces with $2\leq n \leq 6$.

analysisBasis.abstract: A hypersurface $\Sigma \subset\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ is called EDH-stable if it is a critical point of the Euler-Dierkes-Huisken functional $\mathcal{E}_\alpha(\Sigma)=\int_\Sigma|x|^\alpha\, d\mathcal{H}^n$ with nonnegative second variation, which was introduced by Dierkes and Huisken in \cite{[DH-24]}. metadata.title: Smooth local isometric embeddings in dimension four
metadata.abstract: We prove that every smooth four-dimensional Riemannian metric admits, near each point, a local isometric embedding into $\mathbb{R}^{10}$, and that this universal dimension is optimal. A Gram criterion constructs a regular analytic embedding of the Euclidean metric from a rational positive semidefinite tensor obtained by signed evaluations. A specified finite-field minor certifies characteristic regularity. The real-principal-type construction of Nakamura and Maeda gives openness of the metric map on a fixed ball. Rescaling then applies it to arbitrary smooth metrics.
metadata.comment: 8 pages, with ancillary Python scripts for verifying the algebraic certificates

metadata.title: Optimal rational spherical designs on the circle
metadata.abstract: The minimum numbers of points in rational equal-weight spherical designs on the circle are $2304$, $4608$, $9216$, and $9216$ at strengths $4$, $5$, $6$, and $7$, respectively. We construct two nonisometric optimal designs at each strength. At arbitrary strength $t$, we obtain an explicit cardinality divisor $D_t$ with $\log D_t=(1/2+o(1))t\log t$. Applied to the antipodal pairs of a $4608$-point design, Gromov's torus construction gives a flat minimal immersion of $\mathbb{T}^2$ into $S^{4607}$ with $2304$ distinct integral frequencies, attaining Petrunin's sharp Euclidean normal-curvature bound.
metadata.comment: 35 pages. Includes exact verification algorithms and construction certificates

metadata.title: The J-twist of the Dirac operator, spectral Einstein functionals and the noncommutative residue
metadata.abstract: We study spectral Einstein functionals associated with the $J$-twist of the Dirac operator on almost product Riemannian spin manifolds. On closed even-dimensional manifolds, we compute the corresponding noncommutative residue in terms of the Einstein tensor, the curvature of the connection determined by $D_J^2$, and its zero-order endomorphism. For four-dimensional compact manifolds with boundary, we consider two boundary residue functionals obtained by inserting two covariant derivatives in the first factor of the compositions $\pi^+(D_J^{-2})\circ\pi^+(D_J^{-2})$ and $\pi^+(D_J^{-1})\circ\pi^+(D_J^{-3})$. Under the stated collar and almost product structure assumptions, we calculate their interior and boundary contributions and obtain Dąbrowski--Sitarz--Zalecki type formulas. We also present applications of these results in physics and noncommutative geometry, focusing on spectral actions, spectral distance, and mean-curvature boundary contributions.

metadata.title: On maximum volume polytopes inscribed in the sphere
metadata.abstract: We combine degree sequence bounds with a supporting tangent plane method to study maximum volume polytopes inscribed in the sphere $\mathbb S^2$. Building on the vertex-star estimates and combinatorial reductions in Wimmer's dissertation, we determine the exact maximum for ten vertices and the unique maximizing combinatorial type for eleven vertices. Moreover, using explicit computational certificates we identify a unique possible maximizing type for polytopes with thirteen and fifteen vertices, and two possible types for sixteen vertices; this approach also recovers Wimmer's fourteen-vertex combinatorial theorem. Finally, we derive a facial inequality which holds for every degree pattern, and prove that the maximum volume for polytopes with thirty-two vertices is $\frac{2}{3}\sqrt{10(5-\sqrt{5})}$, attained precisely by an inscribed realization of the pentakis dodecahedron, which is the convex hull of the regular icosahedron together with its normalized facet centers. Wimmer had already determined this configuration and its optimality within its own combinatorial type. We also obtain a global degree sequence envelope and a universal affine volume bound.

metadata.title: Euclidean view-obstruction in dimensions eight to ten and the asymptotic deficit
metadata.abstract: The Euclidean view-obstruction problem asks for the critical radius of balls centered at the half-integer lattice that meet every positive ray from the origin. Writing $\Delta_n$ for its square, we determine $\Delta_8=8/17$, $\Delta_9=1087/1980$ and $\Delta_{10}=7/11$ by computer-assisted proofs using Kahlon's seven-dimensional this http URL upper bounds combine full-support subspace averaging, projected lattice coverings and exact finite certificates; dimension ten also requires a finite search through short integer relations. Explicit directions attain all three values, including a ten-dimensional direction previously listed by Gritsenko, Skoruppa and Zagier. In arbitrary dimension, we express their theta-block invariant in geometric normalization and derive the known bounds $c\log(n+1) \le n/12 - \Delta_n \le C\log^3(n+1)$, with repeated coordinates allowed throughout. Thus $\Delta_n \sim n/12$, while the deficit tends to infinity more slowly than every positive power of $n$. The supplementary archive contains the executable verifiers, exact certificates and archived verification records.
metadata.comment: 24 pages. The source code and exact verification data accompany this paper in a separate archive available at this https URL

metadata.title: Parallel domains in $SL_3(\mathbb{R})$ and the ideal triangle reflection group
metadata.abstract: For a given positive triple of flags, we associate an open set, called a parallel domain, in the symmetric space of $SL_3 (\mathbb{R})$ whose boundary is parametrized by three spacelike geodesics of the pseudo-Riemannian symmetric space $SL_3 (\mathbb{R})/GL_2 (\mathbb{R})$. This construction is a higher-rank analog of how three points in the ideal boundary of the hyperbolic plane have an associated ideal triangle. As an application, using the fact that positive triples determine a representation of the ideal triangle reflection group into $SL_3(\mathbb{R})$, we show that these parallel domains are fundamental domains for the group action in the symmetric space. Moreover, using the explicit construction and combinatorial properties of the Farey tessellation, we compute the asymptotics for the critical exponent in the symmetric space and the Hilbert critical exponent as the triple ratio of the triple of flags goes to infinity.

metadata.abstract: Given a compact Lie group acting smoothly and freely on a compact connected manifold, we prove that the space of invariant Riemannian metrics whose symmetry group is precisely the group in question is open dense in that of all invariant metrics provided the orbit space is sufficiently large. This strengthens the author's prior results and recovers Ebin's to the effect that trivial-symmetry Riemannian metrics constitute an open dense set. In the process, the discussion also addresses a number of apparent gaps in said sources, pertaining to the rigidity results in question.

metadata.title: Eaton Triples, Polar Representations, and Lie Triple Systems
metadata.abstract: An Eaton triple consists of a finite dimensional real inner product space, a closed subgroup of its orthogonal group, and a closed convex cone that meets every orbit and satisfies an extremal inner product inequality. In the literature on group majorization and invariant norms it is a standing hypothesis that the triple admits a reduced triple, obtained by restriction to the span of the cone. We prove that this is always the case: the axioms force the span of the cone to be a section of a polar representation, and Gichev's orbit intersection theorem applies. The reduced group is a finite reflection group, crystallographic when the group is connected; Eaton cones are its closed chambers, unique up to the group action; and a compact linear group admits an Eaton cone if and only if its representation is polar with a finite reflection group as Weyl group. For connected groups we construct a Lie triple system on the space, determined by the inner product and the orbits alone, for which the cone is a Weyl chamber; unlike Dadok's orbit equivalence with a symmetric space, it involves no choices.

metadata.title: A note on Positivity and Rigidity for an Expanding Quasi-Local Energy
metadata.abstract: We study positivity and rigidity for an expanding quasi-local energy $E_\lambda$ associated with constantly umbilic initial data $(\Omega,g,k=\lambda g)$, introduced in earlier work [ALP26] as an analogue of the Brown-York energy adapted to an expanding flat de Sitter background. Under nonnegative scalar curvature and suitable boundary assumptions, our previous results established positivity for $\lambda$ below a geometrically determined threshold $\alpha$, while vanishing $E_\lambda$ at $\lambda=\alpha$ forced the boundary to be round. In this paper, we strengthen this endpoint rigidity statement by showing that, if $E_\lambda=0$ when $\lambda=\alpha$, then $(\Omega,g)$ is isometric to a closed Euclidean 3-ball of radius at most $1/\lambda$. The proof combines the rigidity theorem of Shi-Tam for the Brown-York energy with a strict concavity argument. We also construct an explicit counterexample to the positivity and rigidity conjecture formulated in [ALP26], showing that the energy can become negative beyond this threshold and that vanishing energy need not imply rigidity.

metadata.title: The Gorsky-Oblomkov-Rasmussen conjecture over $\mathbb{Q}$
metadata.abstract: We prove a generation theorem for the homology of certain Koszul complexes which naturally arise as the $E^1$ pages of the stable Rasmussen spectral sequence of torus links. Combining this theorem with recent work of Ballinger, Gorsky, Hogancamp, and Wang, we compute the stable Khovanov-Rozansky $\mathfrak{gl}_N$ homology of torus links and determine its Poincaré series, resolving conjectures of Gorsky, Oblomkov, and Rasmussen and their $\mathfrak{gl}_N$ analogs, over $\mathbb{Q}$. Using these results, we determine the Khovanov homology of $T(n,n-1)$ and $T(n,n)$ over $\mathbb{Q}$, confirming conjectures of Shumakovitch and Turner and of the first author, which in turn allows us to compute the Khovanov skein lasagna module of $\overline{\mathbb{CP}^2}$ over $\mathbb{Q}$.

metadata.title: Admissible geometries for Talenti's Pólya--Szegő principle
metadata.abstract: Talenti symmetrization rearranges functions on an open connected set $X\subset\mathbb{R}^N$, endowed with a measure $\mu$ with continuous positive density, along the superlevel sets of a given function $f$. Talenti proved a Pólya--Szegő principle for it, provided that these sets are $\mu$-isoperimetric, have connected boundaries, and are crossed by straight lines of steepest ascent. We show that, if $X$ is convex, these requirements are very rigid: they force the superlevel sets of $f$ to be either parallel half-spaces, or concentric balls, or complements of tubes around an affine subspace of codimension at least two. This identifies the only geometries in which Talenti's Pólya--Szegő principle can be applied. We also prove a family of weighted isoperimetric inequalities in convex cones, showing that complements of tubes around affine subspaces of every codimension at least two do occur.

metadata.title: Compact metric spaces as exponentiable metric compact Hausdorff spaces
metadata.abstract: The class of compact metric spaces (metric spaces which induce a compact topology), despite being an important class of metric spaces, is not closed under many natural constructions. For instance, infinite metric products of compact metric spaces will often fail to induce a compact topology, while on the other hand, the topological product of any family of compact metric spaces is always a compact topological space, evidencing a discrepancy between topological and metric products. The notion of metric compact Hausdorff space -- compact Hausdorff spaces equipped with a lower semi-continuous metric -- provides a class of spaces which keep track of metric data and topological data separately, thereby forming a complete and cocomplete category, while including all compact metric spaces. Our main contribution is that this inclusion can be characterised via universal property: the compact metric spaces are the exponentiable metric compact Hausdorff spaces with respect to a natural monoidal structure on the respective category.

Our main contribution is that this inclusion can be characterised via universal property: the compact metric spaces are the exponentiable metric compact Hausdorff spaces with respect to a natural monoidal structure on the respective category.

metadata.title: Taylor Formulas for H-structures
metadata.abstract: We give a uniform second-order Taylor formula for tensorial Riemannian $H$-structures in Riemannian normal coordinates whose initial frame is $H$-adapted. For a defining multi-tensor $\xi$ with intrinsic torsion $T$, the linear coefficient is $T_q\diamond\xi$, and the quadratic coefficient features the covariant derivative of $T$, its iterated diamond action, and curvature. The formula applies componentwise to tensors of arbitrary type and recovers the known $G_2$ and $\operatorname{Spin}(7)$ expansions. We also give the almost Hermitian specialisation and prove that vanishing of the complete second-order torsion contribution forces the intrinsic torsion to vanish at the centre of the coordinates.

metadata.title: Jacobi fields and Jacobi sections for semisprays on Lie algebroids: transverse variations and equivalences
metadata.abstract: We study the relationship between Jacobi sections and Jacobi fields associated with semisprays on Lie algebroids. First, we characterize compatible transverse variations in terms of Lie algebroid morphisms. This characterization leads to a variational description of Jacobi sections: a section along an integral curve of a semispray is a Jacobi section if and only if it arises as the infinitesimal variation of a compatible transverse variation of a dynamical variation satisfying a suitable condition on its image in the base. We also investigate the relationship between Jacobi sections and Jacobi fields through the anchor map. We prove that every Jacobi section projects to a Jacobi field, and establish a converse when the corresponding base variation is contained in a single leaf of the characteristic foliation.

metadata.title: Twisted pencils of quartics, braid monodromy factorizations, and non-Hopfian Hurwitz curves
metadata.abstract: We study which groups arise as fundamental groups of complements of affine Hurwitz curves. In every such group the product of the meridians is central and maps to the vector of component degrees in homology; this rules out, for instance, the Baumslag-Solitar groups $\operatorname{BS}(p,q)$ with $\lvert p\rvert\neq\lvert q\rvert$, and the groups of links with at least two components and vanishing linking numbers. O. V. Kulikova circumvented this obstruction for $\operatorname{BS}(2,3)$ by passing to the non-Hopfian group $\operatorname{BS}(2,3)\times\mathbb{Z}$, which Vik. S. Kulikov's doubling algorithm realizes in degree $768$. We give an explicit braid monodromy factorization of degree 12 with this group. The corresponding curve is not isotopic to an algebraic curve, yet it is obtained from a union of three quartics in a pencil by a single twist along a circle. More generally, for every closed braid $\hat\beta$ we realize $\pi_1(S^3\setminus\hat\beta)\times\mathbb{Z}$ by an explicit Hurwitz curve, again a twist of a union of quartics in a pencil. In the other direction, a Hurwitz curve with group $\operatorname{BS}(k,k+1)\times\mathbb{Z}$ has degree at least $4$, as every Hurwitz curve consisting of a conic and a line is H-isotopic to an algebraic one, after separation of its critical points. Finally, we show that certain semiholomorphic germs, among them those realizing the generalized Borromean rings, are braided surfaces but not Hurwitz curve germs.

metadata.title: The Escobar Constant for Two-dimensional Disks
metadata.abstract: Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth compact Riemannian surface homeomorphic to a closed disk, with boundary length $L$. We establish sharp upper bounds for its Escobar constant under upper bounds on the Gaussian curvature. If $K_g\leq 0$, then $I(M,g)\leq 2/\pi$, with equality if and only if $(M,g)$ is isometric to a Euclidean disk. If $K_g\leq\kappa$ for some $\kappa>0$, $L<2\pi/\sqrt{\kappa}$, and $\operatorname{Area}_g(M)<2\pi/\kappa$, then $I(M,g)\leq\frac{4}{\sqrt{\kappa}L}\arcsin(\frac{\sqrt{\kappa}L}{2\pi})$, with equality if and only if $(M,g)$ is isometric to the geodesic disk of the same perimeter contained in an open hemisphere of the sphere of constant curvature $\kappa$. We also discuss the higher order Escobar constant for planar domains. In particular, we construct counterexamples to Hassannezhad and Siffert's conjecture.

metadata.title: Stochastic Parallel Transport along Markov Processes: I. General Theory
metadata.abstract: We give a framework for transporting vectors along Markov processes that may have jumps, without assuming a manifold or other specific geometric structure. We prove existence and uniqueness of the resulting transport. In doing so, we develop a theory of vector bundles defined quasi-everywhere, in which the vectors live, and an axiomatic framework for energy forms that determine the bundle and the transport.

metadata.title: Local study of generic dynamical systems on the b-symplectic plane
metadata.abstract: Let $\Gb$ be the group of germs of planar diffeomorphisms, fixing the origin, which preserve the standard b-symplectic form. The group acts on itself, under the usual left-right action and we identify, in the generic case, a simple representative of each orbit, depending on a non-vanishing, univariate, function. We then study the action of $\Gb$ on b-symplectic vector fields. For those fields that do not vanish at the origin, we establish a flow-box type theorem, while, for those that do vanish there, we show that the study of their conjugacy classes reduces to a classification of functions. We present this classification, when the origin is a regular point for these functions, while if it is a critical point, we present the orbits of their 2-jets. Finally, we address the problem of whether an element of $\Gb$ can be realised as the time-1 map of a b-symplectic vector field.

metadata.title: A second-order estimate linear in the gradient for complex Hessian equations
metadata.abstract: We use the maximum principle to prove a second-order estimate with linear dependence on the gradient for the nondegenerate complex Hessian equation on a compact Kähler manifold. The proof combines $C^0$ compactness and a refined concavity inequality with the use of nearby smooth admissible functions. A standard interpolation argument then yields the known uniform gradient and complex Hessian bounds.

metadata.abstract: We compute the Bott--Chern and Aeppli cohomology groups of theta toroidal groups in arbitrary dimensions, obtaining explicit dimension formulas and bases in all bidegrees. For general toroidal groups, we determine the Hausdorff reductions of these cohomology groups and show that they coincide with those of theta toroidal groups. We also compute the Bott--Chern and Aeppli cohomology groups themselves in certain specific bidegrees, without passing to their Hausdorff reductions.

metadata.title: Property $R_\infty$ for Higman$\unicode{x2013}$Thompson Groups
metadata.abstract: We prove that every Higman$\unicode{x2013}$Thompson group $G_{n,r}$, with $n\ge2$ and $r\ge1$, has property $R_\infty$. In particular, every automorphism of Thompson's group $V = G_{2,1}$ has infinitely many twisted conjugacy classes. These results answer questions of Olukoya and of Lins de Araujo, de Oliveira-Tosti and Santos Rego. We also prove that a homeomorphism under which no eventually periodic sequence has a finite orbit has a locally finite centralizer in $G_{n,r}$.

metadata.title: Fractal solutions to the two-dimensional floating body problem
metadata.abstract: In this paper, the first construction of an entire class of two-dimensional fractal bodies that float in water in equilibrium is explicitly given. Their boundaries are described by planar fractal Zindler curves which are constructed using fractal projective hedgehogs. The areas of these bodies are seen to be well-defined and their expression is explicitly computed. To this end, a result concerning the continuity of the Lebesgue measure with respect to the Hausdorff metric for compact sets is given. Furthermore, the Hausdorff dimension $w$ of these fractal curves is shown to coincide with the Hausdorff dimension of the graph of a Weierstrass function associated to the corresponding fractal projective hedgehog. The fractal Zindler curves are proved to have halving chords of constant length that split both the area and the $w$-dimensional Hausdorff measure of the curve into exact halves.

metadata.title: Ricci pseudo symmetric Anisotropic Fluid Spacetime admitting Hyperbolic solitons with Ricci vector field
metadata.abstract: This work focuses on an anisotropic fluid spacetime with these unique forms of the stress-energy tensor associated with radial pressure and a transverse pressure p. In an anisotropic fluid spacetime , we mani- fest curvatures symmetry such as Ricci pseudo-symmetric and prove that Ricci pseudo-symmetric anisotropic fluid spacetime is generalized quasi- Einstein spacetime. We deduce the Einstein gravitational field equation of Ricci pseudo-symmetric anisotropic fluid spacetime. In the framework of pseudo-Riemannian geometry, specifically, we study the quasi-conformal Ricci pseudo-symmetric anisotropic fluid spacetime, which exhibit the dark matter era. Moreover, we discuss the hyperbolic Ricci soliton and Hyperbolic Yamabe soliton on Ricci pseudo-symmetric anisotropic fluid spacetime with a time-like Ricci vector field. Finally, we turn up the char- acteristics of hyperbolic Ricci soliton and hyperbolic Yamabe soliton on Ricci pseudo-symmetric anisotropic fluid spacetime with a time-like Ricci vector field.

metadata.title: Harmonic functions and comparsion geometry for noncompact 3-manifolds with nonnegative scalar curvature
metadata.abstract: In this paper, we establish several sharp comparsion results for noncompact 3-manifolds with nonnegative scalar curvature and with a compact, connected boundary under a boundary mean curvature condition. Then we apply these gradient estimates to establish a Cohn-Vossen type bound for the average of the scalar curvature. This generalizes the work of Colding-Minicozzi \cite{Cold4} and Oronzio \cite{Oro2}.

metadata.title: Global Classification of the Flat Singular Escobar-Yamabe Equation
metadata.abstract: In every dimension $n\geq3$, we classify positive solutions of the flat Escobar--Yamabe equation on the Euclidean half-space with a possible isolated boundary singularity at the origin. Solutions with a removable singularity are boundary bubbles. Up to dilation, the nonremovable solutions are the cylindrical solution and a family of periodic Delaunay solutions uniquely parametrized by the necksize $\epsilon \in (0,1)$, the minimum of the normalized boundary trace. In each fundamental period $T_\epsilon$, the trace has exactly two critical points, a nondegenerate minimum and a nondegenerate maximum. The period and the solution centered at the trace minimum and rescaled to period one depend smoothly on $\epsilon$. As $\epsilon \to 0$, $T_\epsilon = \frac{4}{n-2}\log(1/\epsilon)+O(1)$. As $\epsilon \to 1$, the solutions converge to the cylindrical solution and their periods tend to that of its linearized oscillation. We use uniqueness in the odd and even classes for linear Robin equations to obtain reflection symmetry and continuation in the necksize.

metadata.title: Dimension reduction by bi-Hölder maps
metadata.abstract: The Hölder dimension of a metric space is the infimum of its Hausdorff dimension over all bi-Hölder changes of the metric. Colvin asked whether it can take noninteger values. We show that every metric space of finite upper box dimension has integer Hölder dimension. For a bounded subset of a Euclidean space, the dimension reduction is carried out by a global homeomorphism of the ambient space, built from randomly translated singular functions, which brings the Hausdorff dimension of the set arbitrarily close to its integer part.

metadata.title: Smooth Rigidity Near Extremal Horizons
metadata.abstract: The Einstein equations constrain the transverse Taylor series at a degenerate Killing horizon, but even complete knowledge of that series need not determine a smooth spacetime: a nonzero difference can vanish to every order at the horizon. We show that this ambiguity disappears when the limiting metric on the space of Killing orbits admits a spacelike graph over a compact horizon section. In dimensions $d\geq4$, smooth vacuum Einstein germs with the same marked transverse jets are then locally isometric on a two-sided neighborhood of the whole section. The proof combines a terminal wave-map gauge with energy estimates on the orbit cylinder and yields a finite weighted matching criterion. For unwarped horizons with positive-Einstein sections, a condition on the full Lichnerowicz spectrum reduces the smooth classification to parallel first transverse data. All such data have convergent multiwarped Einstein realizations, including examples whose sections have negative sectional-curvature directions. We also obtain a finite-regularity version for round sections. The continuation argument extends to four-dimensional Einstein--Maxwell theory and gives smooth charged-Nariai rigidity. Finally, rotating Nariai data admit the required spacelike graph throughout the regular branch; an all-order tensor estimate yields smooth Kerr--de Sitter or rotating-Nariai rigidity for $a^2/r_0^2\leq1/8$, without assuming ambient axial symmetry.

metadata.title: Bounded Spaces without a Geodesic in the Gromov-Hausdorff Class
metadata.abstract: We construct two countable complete bounded metric spaces at Gromov-Hausdorff distance $1/4$ with no midpoint and hence no shortest curve between them. The proof uses the local existence of optimal correspondences near a space with finitely many self-correspondences of distortion below a fixed positive threshold, each of which is the graph of a bijection.

metadata.title: No regular icosahedron has a rational point on every face: a proof checked in Lean
metadata.abstract: We prove that no regular icosahedron in $\mathbb{R}^3$ has a point with rational coordinates on each of its twenty closed faces, in every position, size and orientation, reflections included. This answers a question of I. Bogdanov on MathOverflow. A field automorphism of $\mathbb{C}$ that sends $\sqrt5$ to $-\sqrt5$ reduces the problem to the following statement: for every complex orthogonal $3\times3$ matrix $T$ some real linear combination of $\mathrm{Re}\,T$ and $\mathrm{Im}\,T$ separates ten intervals determined by the faces. We prove this statement by a computer-assisted case analysis over rational parametrizations of rotation frames, in which every inequality is an exact polynomial bound over $\mathbb{Z}[\varphi]$, $\varphi=(1+\sqrt5)/2$; no floating-point arithmetic and no Lipschitz estimates are used. The whole argument, including the $48$ certificates, is formalized in the Lean 4 proof assistant with Mathlib and checked by the Lean kernel; the main theorem depends only on the standard axioms. The mathematical argument and the formalization were produced by AI systems (OpenAI Codex and Anthropic Claude) under the direction of the author; see the statement at the end of the paper.

metadata.title: Geometric Endpoints, Global Trajectories, and Teichmüller Projection for the Möbius-Invariant Willmore Flow
metadata.abstract: We study endpoints and conformal projection of the Möbius-invariant Willmore flow in the round three-sphere. Under uniform nonumbilicity or an integrable weighted condition, image-measure transport yields a unique finite-time integral-varifold limit. Reduced Hopf trajectories have unique anchored finite-time profile and marked conformal endpoints at arbitrary energy. Every smooth global reduced trajectory converges smoothly modulo reparametrization to an elastic profile, with quantitative rates and finite dissipation length. We compute the differential of the conformal-class projection along reduced trajectories and prove that its maximal rank persists at every finite time when it holds initially. Near the Clifford torus, Hopf tori with the same marked conformal type can have noncollinear projected velocities, ruling out a common autonomous Teichmüller equation even after positive time recalibrations.

analysisBasis.abstract: We study endpoints and conformal projection of the Möbius-invariant Willmore flow in the round three-sphere. Under uniform nonumbilicity or an integrable weighted condition, image-measure transport yields a unique finite-time integral-varifold limit. Reduced Hopf trajectories have unique anchored finite-time profile and marked conformal endpoints at arbitrary energy. Every smooth global reduced trajectory converges smoothly modulo reparametrization to an elastic profile, with quantitative rates and finite dissipation length. We compute the differential of the conformal-class projection along reduced trajectories and prove that its maximal rank persists at every finite time when it holds initially. Near the Clifford torus, Hopf tori with the same marked conformal type can have noncollinear projected velocities, ruling out a common autonomous Teichmüller equation even after positive time recalibrations.

metadata.title: The sharp bound on the distance between the centers of mass of a convex body and its boundary
metadata.abstract: We prove that the distance between the centers of mass $c(K)$ and $c(\partial K)$ of a convex body $K$ and its boundary $\partial K$, respectively, does not exceed $ D_n$ times the width of $K$ in the direction of the vector joining $c(\partial K)$ and $c(K)$. The constant $D_n$ is optimal and coincides with the sharp constant in the problem of bounding the distance between the orthogonal projection of the centroid of a convex body onto a hyperplane and the centroid of its orthogonal projection onto that hyperplane.

metadata.title: Collapsing flat manifolds with totally geodesic boundary
metadata.abstract: We study volume collapse of compact connected flat manifolds with nonempty totally geodesic boundary and uniformly bounded diameter. We prove subsequential Gromov--Hausdorff convergence to compact flat orbifolds, allowing reflector loci, and describe the limit using the canonical involutions of the doubles. We distinguish the cases in which the maximal distance to the boundary tends to zero or to a positive limit, and classify all possible limits in dimension three.

metadata.title: Geometric Rigidity of Manifolds Admitting $m$-Modified Conformal Vector Fields
metadata.abstract: We establish certain integral inequalities for $m$-modified conformal vector fields on compact Riemannian manifolds and derive corresponding triviality and rigidity results. We further obtain integrability conditions for such vector fields and establish an extended Bourguignon-Ezin identity. We then prove that a compact Riemannian manifold admitting a non-trivial closed $m$-modified conformal vector field is isometric to a round sphere under either a constant scalar curvature and positive Ricci curvature assumption or a suitable bound on the Ricci curvature involving the first nonzero eigenvalue of the Laplace operator. As a consequence, we obtain an extension of a classical sphere characterization result of Yano and Nagano to the corresponding result for a non trivial $m$-modified conformal vector field assumed closed. Finally, we consider a complete Kähler manifold admitting a closed $m$-modified conformal vector field $V$, and show that $V$ is $m$-modified Killing and around a non-zero point of $V$ the manifold splits as the product of the complex Euclidean plane $\mathbb{C}$ and a complete Kähler manifold.

metadata.title: The topology of end-periodic smoothing operators
metadata.abstract: We develop an algebra of smoothing operators adapted to the geometry of end-periodic manifolds. We extend the renormalized trace and trace defect formula of Mrowka-Ruberman-Saveliev to this algebra, and establish a Fredholm criterion and winding-number index formula for smoothing perturbations of the identity. Our main result computes the homotopy groups of the associated end-periodic smoothing group. This provides a foundation for future work on relative index theory for families of end-periodic differential operators.

metadata.title: Isoperimetric comparison for surfaces with nonnegative curvature and uniformly convex boundary
metadata.abstract: We establish a sharp relative isoperimetric comparison for compact surfaces with nonnegative Gaussian curvature and smooth nonempty boundary whose geodesic curvature is at least 1. We prove that the normalized relative isoperimetric profile for such a surface is bounded below by that of the Euclidean unit disk, with equality holding at some area fraction in (0,1) if and only if the surface is isometric to the unit disk. The proof uses a differential comparison argument for the isoperimetric profile, based on a suitable non-constant normal variation of isoperimetric curves inspired by the model geometry.

analysisBasis.abstract: We establish a sharp relative isoperimetric comparison for compact surfaces with nonnegative Gaussian curvature and smooth nonempty boundary whose geodesic curvature is at least 1. We prove that the normalized relative isoperimetric profile for such a surface is bounded below by that of the Euclidean unit disk, with equality holding at some area fraction in (0,1) if and only if the surface is isometric to the unit disk. The proof uses a differential comparison argument for the isoperimetric profile, based on a suitable non-constant normal variation of isoperimetric curves inspired by the model geometry.

metadata.title: A Cheeger-Müller Theorem For Flat Superconnections
metadata.abstract: For a flat superconnection ${\mathbb{A}}$ on a ${\mathbb{Z}}_2$-graded vector bundle $E$ over a closed oriented odd-dimensional manifold $M$, we prove a Cheeger-Müller type theorem as proposed by Arias Abad and Schätz. Namely, that the topological Reidemeister norm of ${\mathbb{A}}$ as defined by them equals the Ray-Singer metric defined by Mathai and Wu. The main step proves an analytic reduction result identified by Arias Abad and Schätz and formulated as a conjecture by the author, that the Ray-Singer metric coincides with that of the fibrewise cohomology $H(E,\partial)$ with its Gauss-Manin connection, where $\partial$ is the component of ${\mathbb{A}}$ of form degree zero, under the Knudsen-Mumford isomorphism associated to the form-degree spectral sequence. As an application, we consider Goette's Morse flat superconnection of a fibrewise Morse function on a fibre bundle with even-dimensional fibres over an oriented odd-dimensional base.

metadata.title: Curvature estimates for shrinking gradient Ricci solitons
metadata.abstract: Suppose $(M^5,g,f)$ is a complete gradient shrinking Ricci soliton with bounded scalar curvature. We prove that if $\nu(g)>-\log 2$, then its Riemannian curvature is bounded. The proof uses curvature blow-up, a local Ricci estimate, and the splitting given by the rescaled potential. An entropy estimate then allows us to apply the volume-ratio gap theorem for Ricci-flat four-manifolds.

metadata.title: On evolution of mean curvature and minimal areas in general codimension for inverse problems
metadata.abstract: Many seemingly standard formulas for the evolution of the mean curvature vector in higher codimension assume only normal variations, which are ill-suited for analyzing the evolution of submanifolds- with-boundary whose boundaries may not be moving orthogonally at each time. Such situations arise when one considers inverse problems for minimal areas, for example, where such boundaries are confined to a larger ambient boundary. In this note, we provide coordinate-free identities for use in such problems, including higher order derivatives of mean curvature. We translate these identities to some of the existing inverse problem literature in codimension one. We also hope readers may find the computational framework helpful in other situations arising in geometric analysis.

metadata.title: Compact branch sets and injectivity of proper branched coverings
metadata.abstract: In this paper, we show that a proper continuous open discrete map from the open unit ball $B^n$ onto a domain in $\R^n$ with $n\geq5$ is a homeomorphism whenever its branch set is compact. This answers Vuorinen's question affirmatively in every dimension $n\ge5.$ In dimension four, we also show that, under the additional assumption of quasiregularity, the map is a quasiconformal homeomorphism. Together with the three-dimensional theorem of Kauranen, Luisto and Tengvall, these results answer the quasiregular question posed as Problem~7.66 in the collections of Barth--Brannan--Hayman and Hayman--Lingham in every dimension $n\ge3$.

metadata.title: Conical Singularities of Toda Solutions with One Finite-Energy Component and Classification on the Punctured Plane
metadata.abstract: We study Toda systems associated with arbitrary complex simple Lie algebras. For solutions on a punctured disc, we prove that finite energy of at least one component near the puncture forces every component to have a conical singularity there. On the punctured plane, we give a geometric formulation and proof of the Lin--Nie--Wei classification of solutions with prescribed cone exponents at the origin and finite total energy in at least one component. We express the parameter space as the complex centralizer of the monodromy modulo a maximal compact subgroup. We also recover the formulas of Karmakar--Lin--Nie--Wei for the cone exponents at infinity and the total energies of the components.

metadata.title: Infinitude of integral Hitchin representations of Coxeter polygons
metadata.abstract: We prove that there are infinitely many Hitchin $\operatorname{SL}^\pm(3, \mathbb Z)$-representations of a Coxeter $n$-gon($n \geq 9$) group whose boundary parameters are fixed. metadata.title: Lower bound of the Calabi functional and non-Archimedean K-energy
metadata.abstract: We prove Donaldson's conjecture which describes the infimum of the Calabi functional by the normalized non-Archimedean K-energy. The proof makes use of proximal equation for the K-energy. To obtain approximate smooth solutions, a continuity path of prescribed scalar curvature equation is coupled with a version of Chen's $\e$-subgeodesic. It does not require a global smooth solution to the Calabi flow.

metadata.title: Curve theory in $S^2\times S^2$ with applications to ruled surfaces in $S^3$
metadata.abstract: The Riemannian product $S^2\times S^2$ of two unit spheres admits several important geometric interpretations. It can be identified both with the complex quadric $Q^2$ and with the space $\mathcal{L}(S^3)$ of oriented geodesics in the unit $3$-sphere $S^3$. In this paper, we first develop a unified framework for the geometry of curves in $S^2\times S^2$. We introduce projection-regular curves in $S^2\times S^2$ and their curvature data, and prove a congruence theorem for these curves. As an application of this framework, regarding $S^2\times S^2$ as the complex quadric $Q^2$, we classify Kähler magnetic geodesics associated with the product Kähler--Einstein structure. For closed generic projection-regular curves, we establish a sharp Fenchel-type inequality. We then identify $S^2\times S^2$ with the space $\mathcal{L}(S^3)$ of oriented geodesics in the unit $3$-sphere $S^3$ and apply our curve theory to ruled surfaces in $S^3$. In particular, we prove that every nonsingular closed generic projection-regular ruled surface attaining equality in the Fenchel-type inequality is an embedded torus.

metadata.title: An invariant higher index pairing under Morita equivalence for proper étale groupoids
metadata.abstract: For suitable proper étale groupoids, we study a part of the higher index that is invariant under Morita equivalence. We capture this part by a pairing between cyclic homology classes associated with isotropy groups and cyclic cohomology classes of the groupoid convolution algebra. We show that the pushforward is compatible with the maps induced by essential equivalences. This gives a numerical invariant depending only on the Morita equivalence class of the groupoid. In the case of a finite group action, we relate the resulting pairing to the equivariant index and to the Atiyah-Bott fixed-point formula.

metadata.title: Integrable Measure Equivalence and Gromov's conjecture on nilpotent groups
metadata.abstract: In this article we prove a well-known conjecture due to M. Gromov that if two infinite finitely generated torsion free nilpotent groups $\Gamma$ and $\Lambda$ are Quasi-isometric, then their Mal'cev Completions are isomorphic as Lie groups. We prove this result in more general set-up. We prove that if two infinite finitely generated torsion free nilpotent groups $\Gamma$ and $\Lambda$ are Integrable Measure Equivalent, then the Mal'cev completions of $\Gamma$ and $\Lambda$ are isomorphic as Lie groups. Equivalently, using Y. Shalom's result we prove that two infinite countable torsion free nilpotent groups $\Gamma$ and $\Lambda$ are Integrable Measure Equivalent if and only if $\Gamma$ and $\Lambda$ are quasi-isometric if and only if the Mal'cev Completions of $\Gamma$ and $\Lambda$ are isomorphic as Lie groups. Moreover, we discuss some applications of our main theorem to lifting of quasi-isometric embedding from $\Gamma$ to $\Lambda$ to a homo-morphism between their Mal'cev completions, and betti numbers of nilpotent groups.

metadata.title: Quasipositive and almost positive sectional curvature on finite quotients of Wallach spaces
metadata.abstract: We construct nonnegatively curved metrics on the cyclic and full permutation quotients of the Wallach flag manifolds in dimensions $6$, $12$, and $24$. The metrics are quasipositively curved in all three dimensions and almost positively curved in dimensions $12$ and $24$. The cyclic quotients are orientable with fundamental group $C_3$, and their further full permutation quotients have fundamental group $S_3$; none admits any metric of everywhere positive sectional curvature. For the almost-positive metrics we describe every zero-curvature plane and prove that the zero-point loci have Hausdorff dimensions exactly $11$ and $23$, respectively. A one-step deformation has, in each dimension, an explicit zero locus with nonempty interior. Further nested deformations reduce it to a measure-zero set while leaving a common codimension-one stratum. The argument combines normal forms for horizontal commuting planes with quaternionic rank conditions and a dimension estimate for commuting compressions of skew-symmetric operators. We also determine the possible degrees of arbitrary free finite quotients of the three flag covers and derive order bounds for fundamental groups when the Euler characteristic is nonzero. We have used ChatGPT-6-astra for mathematical exploration and verified and rewritten all the results.

metadata.title: Branched real projective structures on surfaces, cyclic Higgs Bundles and Anosov representations
metadata.abstract: We use the theory of $3$-cyclic $\mathrm{SL}(3,\mathbb{R})$-Higgs bundles to study real branched projective structures on compact surfaces recently introduced by the authors. After fixing a Riemann surface structure on $S$, the Higgs bundle approach allows us, on the one hand, to construct branched structures with prescribed branching data and, on the other hand, to introduce new classes of such structures. The latter are directly related to singular hyperbolic affine spheres and carry a Blaschke metric with conical singularities. In the final part of the paper, using different methods, we prove that every Anosov surface group representation into $\mathrm{SL}(3,\mathbb{R})$ is either Hitchin or belongs to the Barbot component. As a by-product, we obtain that some of the representations associated with the branched structures constructed above are not Anosov.

analysisBasis.abstract: We use the theory of $3$-cyclic $\mathrm{SL}(3,\mathbb{R})$-Higgs bundles to study real branched projective structures on compact surfaces recently introduced by the authors. After fixing a Riemann surface structure on $S$, the Higgs bundle approach allows us, on the one hand, to construct branched structures with prescribed branching data and, on the other hand, to introduce new classes of such structures. The latter are directly related to singular hyperbolic affine spheres and carry a Blaschke metric with conical singularities. In the final part of the paper, using different methods, we prove that every Anosov surface group representation into $\mathrm{SL}(3,\mathbb{R})$ is either Hitchin or belongs to the Barbot component. As a by-product, we obtain that some of the representations associated with the branched structures constructed above are not Anosov.

metadata.title: Lie-Lions brackets of nonlocal vector fields
metadata.abstract: We study nonlocal vector fields on the space of probability measures with finite second moment. Using Lions derivatives, we define their Lie-Lions bracket, which adds to the spatial Lie bracket a correction due to the evolution of the law, and prove that its vanishing is equivalent to commutation of the global flows, under first-order regularity and linear growth assumptions. We then construct a Lie algebra of complete polynomial nonlocal fields. For this class, we establish commutator and second-order Baker-Campbell-Hausdorff formulas with cubic remainders in the Wasserstein distance $W_2$, controlled by the second moment and uniform in the number of particles. The proofs rely on finite-particle realizations, which preserve the bracket and jointly determine the nonlocal field. We also obtain uniform estimates for smooth bounded kernels and a Leibniz rule for the action of polynomial fields on polynomial observables. Examples from collective dynamics show that the vanishing of the spatial bracket at a fixed law is neither necessary nor sufficient for commutation. They concern symmetries, aggregation-dependent rotation, synchronization, the transmission of a turn along a hierarchy, effective three-body interactions and occupancy-dependent circulation.

metadata.title: Almost complex structures on triple blow-ups
metadata.abstract: We show that for certain smooth 4-manifolds, almost complex structures on its triple blow-up induce all its spin$^c$ structures with a non-negative-dimensional Seiberg-Witten moduli space. Since this includes all basic classes, our result provides an approximation to the simple type conjecture. Moreover, we expand a result by Dieter Kotschick showing that every finitely presented group is the fundamental group of an almost complex 4-manifold. We show that it can furthermore be chosen to have every even integer as the virtual dimension of the Seiberg-Witten moduli space of a spin$^c$ structure.

metadata.title: Convergence of finite element exterior calculus for the Hodge-Dirac and Hodge-Laplace problems on closed Riemannian manifolds
metadata.abstract: We prove that the finite element exterior calculus (FEEC) approximation to the Hodge-Dirac and Hodge-Laplace problems on any closed oriented Riemannian manifold converges. Its approximate solutions, together with their exterior derivatives, converge to the continuum solutions for every source, and at the rate of the mesh size when the source and its codifferential are square integrable. We use Licht's estimate for the FEEC approximation of forms with one square-integrable derivative by finite element forms. We combine this with a new abstract error bound for approximations of Hilbert complexes. This bound uses a version of Di Pietro and Droniou's third Strang lemma. To apply these estimates, we show that every closed manifold admits a family of arbitrarily fine triangulations whose shapes stay uniformly under control.

metadata.title: Scalar curvature deformation of isoparametric tubes
metadata.abstract: We resolve Ge's local scalar curvature rigidity conjecture for spherical isoparametric tubes. The conjecture fails throughout its stated radius range for families with at least two distinct principal curvatures, via arbitrarily small smooth deformations supported in any regular annulus. Geodesic balls of radius less than $\frac{\pi}{2}$ are locally rigid under $C^2$ smallness. We also prescribe sufficiently small smooth nonradial scalar-curvature increments with fixed compact interior support, under antipodal symmetry for families with 2, 4, or 6 distinct principal curvatures and without symmetry for families with 3 distinct principal curvatures.

metadata.title: Negative normal degree and holomorphic sectional curvature pinching
metadata.abstract: We obtain an upper bound for the local holomorphic sectional curvature pinching of a Kähler manifold containing a smooth rational curve of negative total normal degree. As an application, we prove that a compact Kähler surface with positive holomorphic sectional curvature and local pinching constant at least $1/9$ is biholomorphic to $\mathbb{CP}^2$, $\mathbb{CP}^1\times\mathbb{CP}^1$, or the first Hirzebruch surface $\mathbb F_1$. For pinching strictly greater than $1/9$, only the first two possibilities occur, confirming a conjecture of Yang and Zheng. We also determine the optimal local pinching constants on $\mathbb F_1$ and $\mathbb F_2$.

metadata.title: Geodesic connectedness of globally hyperbolic spacetimes with a causal Killing vector field
metadata.abstract: We characterize the existence of a geodesic joining two prescribed points of a globally hyperbolic spacetime $(M,g)$ admitting a complete causal Killing vector field $K$ and a complete smooth spacelike Cauchy hypersurface $S$. We prove that two points $p,q\in M$ are joined by a geodesic if and only if there exists an $H^1$ curve $\gamma$ from $p$ to $q$ such that $g(\dot\gamma,K)$ is constant almost everywhere. The statement is intrinsic and allows $K$ to be timelike at some points and lightlike at others. A global splitting induced by the flow of $K$ is used in the proof, but no global bounds on the metric coefficients are imposed. The proof relies on stationary perturbations of $(M,g)$, whose relevant compactness properties follow from global hyperbolicity of $g$, and on uniform estimates based on an integral admissibility condition and a Glaeser-type inequality. Two examples illustrate geodesic connectedness and the obstruction detected by the characterization.

metadata.title: Cube tilings, partition counters, and the Calkin--Wilf and Kepler trees
metadata.abstract: A tiling of the integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$ by translates of the discrete cube $K_d=\{0,1\}^d$ cuts every translate $K_d+x$ into subcubes. We study the function $\ell(x)$ counting these parts. Its sum over every translate of $K_d$ equals $3^d$, for an arbitrary translation set. For lattice tilings with a triangular basis we obtain a dimension-reduction formula, and we describe every cocyclic lattice by a single normalized congruence. Along a cyclic generator, the counter of a signed bidiagonal lattice is a row of Stern's diatomic sequence; pairs of counter values realize the Calkin--Wilf tree, and complementary binary words realize the Kepler tree. For the binary lattice, the translated counter labelings of the cube carry generating face partitions, supplied by the tiling itself, which force the levels of the Kepler tree, and every nontrivial face partition has a unique lamination direction. Using finite Fourier analysis we prove that the ordered cyclic profile determines a standard cocyclic cube tiling lattice up to coordinate reflections. For lattices tiling by discrete boxes we determine exactly when the analogous statement holds.

metadata.title: Odd realisation numbers of rigid graphs
metadata.abstract: Determining the number of realisations of a rigid graph for a specific choice of edge lengths is a fundamental problem in discrete geometry. Gortler, Healy and Thurston showed that the number of real realisations of a generic framework is always even or equal to one. Despite being rare, there do exist graphs whose number of complex realisations is odd and not equal to one. In this article, we exhibit two necessary conditions for a rigid graph to have an odd realisation number other than one. We also provide an infinite family of rigid graphs with an odd realisation number other than one.

metadata.title: Real quadratic fields and finite quantum dilogarithms II: traces of quantum modular cocycles
metadata.abstract: We study traces of quantum modular cocycles at fixed points of hyperbolic elements $\gamma\in\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$, formulate an algebraicity conjecture for these traces, and prove it for the cocycles associated to 1-dimensional state-integrals. In addition, we analyse a finite TQFT associated with $\gamma$ and conjecture that its invariants for 3-manifolds agree with the traces of their $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ quantum modular cocycles. The finite TQFTs predict a yet-to-be-defined motive with cohomology equipped with a $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$-degree grading and a $\mathbb{Z}$-weight grading coming from a version of the Riemann hypothesis, which suggests a similar grading should exist for an extension of the Kauffman bracket skein module, for the framed $\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})$ Floer cohomology of Abouzaid--Manolescu, and for the quantum modular cocycle. This leads to surprising additive identities among algebraic units, which we confirm for the complement of the simplest hyperbolic knot $4_1$, as well as for $S^1 \times \Sigma_g$ for a closed genus $g$ surface.

metadata.title: The symmetric Gaussian isoperimetric problem in the plane
metadata.abstract: We resolve the symmetric Gaussian isoperimetric conjecture in the plane: every minimizer of Gaussian perimeter among centrally symmetric sets of prescribed Gaussian measure is a centered ball, a symmetric strip, or the complement of one of these sets. A quadrant-reflection argument reduces the problem to unconditional sets. The planar structural results of Barchiesi, Cagnetti and Julin then leave only a noncircular strictly convex stationary oval. We exclude this oval by an explicit volume-preserving and perimeter-decreasing linear deformation, which geometrically corresponds to an "unconditional squeezing". More generally, without requiring any symmetry assumptions, we show that any noncircular closed embedded $\lambda$-self-shrinker is always unstable via linear deformations. We also record a reduction to the unconditional case in dimension three, using an orthogonal equipartition theorem of Musin.

metadata.title: Branch Obstructions for Area-Minimizing Currents and Flat Critical Points of Weakly-Conformal Maps
metadata.abstract: We study two problems motivated by the local geometry of conformal $\phi$-curves. First, let $T$ be a $k$-dimensional locally area-minimizing integral current in Euclidean space, with $k\geq3$, codimension at least two, no boundary, and a locally conformally flat induced metric on $\operatorname{reg} T$. We prove the following branch obstruction: at any rapid-decay branch point whose planar frequency differs from $2$, every nonzero cyclic component of every cylindrical normalized tangent function has repetition multiplicity at least two. Consequently, the nonintegral-frequency points of densities $2$ and $3$ in the rapid-decay branch set have Hausdorff dimension at most $k-3$. On the full branch set, they have zero $\mathcal H^{k-2}$ measure. These conclusions apply to Euclidean image currents of conformal $\phi$-curves with locally conformally flat domains, provided the image currents satisfy the stated hypotheses. Second, for $C^j$ weakly-conformal maps between smooth Riemannian manifolds, with domain dimension $k\geq3$ and $j\geq2$, we prove that all derivatives of orders $1$ through $j$ vanish at every critical point. As a consequence, for smooth weakly-conformal maps with connected domain, we establish a curvature condition under which the map is constant or has no critical points. The flatness and continuation results apply in particular to conformal $\phi$-curves with the corresponding regularity and curvature assumptions. Finally, we examine the Borůvka cone, which illustrates the role of regularity and the distinction between critical points and branch points.

metadata.title: Sets of reach $R$ are $\operatorname{CAT}\left( 1/R^2\right)$
metadata.abstract: Positive reach underpins many results in computational geometry and topology. It is used for triangulation criteria, topological inference, and manifold learning. The geometric properties of these sets have therefore been studied intensely. In this paper we focus on the intrinsic metric properties of sets of positive reach. In particular we give an elementary proof of the fact that (closed) sets of reach at least $R$ are $\operatorname{CAT}(1/R^2)$. This fact was established earlier by Alexander and Bishop, using quite significant machinery. The fact that a space is $\operatorname{CAT}(1/R^2)$ offers many advantages, such as the uniqueness and continuity of sufficiently short geodesics, the existence of Fr{é}chet means and by extension the Rips based homotopy reconstruction of Hausmann is available.
